title: Ella's earliest recordings and A-Tisket, A-Tasket
summary: They sort out Ella's first records, her Goodman session, and how A-Tisket, A-Tasket made her popular.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Let me just ask you what were the earliest recordings with Ella Fitzgerald and the band. Did you say she recorded with Goodman before she recorded with you?
Right. But what was her first recording with you, A Tisket, A Tasket?

No, no. She record -- she record a song much before that. We went to the -- we went to Boston to the Le Vaggi -- Le Vaggi Restaurant, and I think it was in '36, I think it was. Yeah, in '36, because I just got through -- late '36, '36 or -7. I'm bad on dates. But that -- just like you said, that can be checked.

Uh-huh. And she just got through writing that song. And we used to play that song in there. That's -- and everybody used to ask for that song half a dozen times a night. And then we give them the other recording of we took from Decca Two-Foot-Baker (phonetic).
And she recorded with Goodman, I think it's Good Night, My Love. I think that's the tune that she recorded with Goodman, something like that. When she recorded with Goodman, She ain't popular yet.
What is it that really made her popular, A Tisket, A Tasket?
A Tisket, A Tasket. That was real big. That was real big. That would turn the trick.
